title: Staged degradation & backfill routing — control plane playbook and architecture notes
content:
Purpose:
This note defines a pragmatic, staged approach for handling regional or global inference degradations by combining routing policy adjustments with temporary backfill strategies. It mixes operational runbook steps with architecture-level considerations so on-call engineers can make safe, reversible changes while preserving SLOs and minimizing user impact.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to control-plane-driven routing for text-generation/chat endpoints and model variants across multiple regions (eg. us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-south-1).
- Control plane can atomically update routing weights, enable short-lived fallbacks (model variant or hosted shim), and trigger capacity actions via autoscale APIs.
- Backfill options: CPU-quantized variant, lower-precision quantized GPU variant, hosted API proxy. Each backfill has different cost/latency/quality tradeoffs.
- Goal: preserve availability first, then latency SLOs, then quality. Prefer staged actions over blunt cutovers.

Key signals (detection):
- Region-level 5m rolling error rate > 2% for production route OR 99th latency > 1.5x SLO for 3 consecutive 1m buckets.
- Persistent control-plane store write latency > 500ms affecting routing updates.
- Autoscaler failing to provision GPU nodes for > 10m.
- KV-cache invalidation storm: large spike in model cache misses (> 3x baseline) with token-per-request increase.
- Synthetic checks failing for a regional control endpoint (health probe failures > 2/3).

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm alerts and scope: check grafana (routes-per-region, error/retry counts, 99/95/50 latencies), control-plane audit logs, and infra provider status.
2) Page SRE + platform on-call, mark timeline in incident channel.
3) Determine impact class: localized region (impacting <= 2% traffic), multi-region (>= 20%), or global routing/control-plane (control-plane degraded).
4) If control-plane itself is healthy but region is degraded, proceed with routing-stage plan. If control-plane is degraded, focus on control-plane recovery and use manual operator fallbacks described below.

Staged response pattern (recommended order):
Stage 0 - observation and safety locks:
- Do not push permanent config changes. Enable temporary lock to prevent automated rollouts.
- Enable increased sampling for traces/requests for the affected route to collect evidence (retain short TTL).

Stage 1 - soft reweight (10–25% incremental) to other healthy regions:
- Target: reduce tail pressure in degraded region while preserving user affinity where possible.
- Mechanism: control-plane API call to apply a delta reweight for 5m rolling window.
- Example command (operator):
  curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/adjust" -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${OPERATOR_TOKEN}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","change":{"type":"delta","by_region":{"us-east-1":-0.15,"eu-west-1":0.15}},"ttl_seconds":300}'
- Verify: expected traffic change observed in 1–2 1m buckets. If errors fall and latency improves, hold and monitor.

Stage 2 - progressive reweight + model variant backfill (if Stage 1 insufficient after 10–15m):
- If tail latency or errors remain elevated, increase reweight up to 50% away from unhealthy region.
- Simultaneously enable a backfill model in the degraded region to handle remaining traffic:
  - Options: CPU-quantized model variant (fast to start, high latency), low-precision GPU variant (medium quality, cheaper GPU), or hosted-api-proxy fallback (external-hosted).
  - Policy: prefer local backfill variant over cross-region routing if cross-region latency would exceed SLO for a majority of requests.
- Command pattern to enable backfill (example):
  curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/variants/enable" -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${OPERATOR_TOKEN}' -d '{"region":"us-east-1","model":"gptx-3-small-cpu-backfill","route":"/v1/generate","weight":0.2,"ttl_seconds":1800}'
- Note: track per-variant quality metrics; flag if semantic regression > 5% vs baseline on the most critical prompt set.

Stage 3 - temporary cross-region steer and throttling:
- If local backfill worsens user experience or is unavailable, steer more aggressively to other regions but add client-facing throttles to protect token-cost and overall system stability.
- Apply token-rate limit policy for the route or downgrade sampling for long-context requests.
- Use gradual windowed steering to avoid flapping.

Stage 4 - emergency hosted-proxy fallback (last resort):
- Enable hosted-api-proxy for a small percentage (<= 20%) of traffic if both local backfill and cross-region steering fail. Clearly note privacy and data-handling implications and only use when permitted by customer tenancy rules.
- Record each activation in the incident timeline and capture request samples for quality checks.

Stage 5 - capacity remediation & durable fixes:
- If incident persists > 1h, trigger capacity allocation playbook: escalate to infra, request GPU node pool expansion, or enable a burst capacity reserve. Use terraform/infra-ops runbook for manual capacity if autoscaler failed.
- Implement long-lived routing changes only after a full regression and QA cycle.

Control plane considerations and safe practices:
- Prefer TTL-limited routing deltas over permanent weight changes when responding to incidents. This ensures automatic rollback in case of human error.
- All operator-initiated weight changes must be annotated in control-plane audit logs and the incident channel with the reason and expected TTL.
- Use canary keying: for any backfill variant add a short-lived canary bucket (1% traffic) to check quality before increasing weight.
- Avoid simultaneous manual changes from multiple humans — use a single operator with a deputy to acknowledge each step.

Model compatibility & quality constraints:
- Before enabling a backfill variant, verify tokenization parity and output schema. For chat endpoints, confirm system messages and function calling remain compatible.
- Annotate any known differences in the incident notes (eg. 'cpu-backfill has different stop-token behaviour for streaming').

Edge-case scenarios (examples and tailored actions):
A) KV-cache invalidation storm in eu-west-1:
- Symptoms: sudden spike in cold cache misses, per-request token counts increase, disk I/O on cache nodes high.
- Action: immediately reweight 20–40% off eu-west-1 and enable local CPU fallback for long-context requests. Rotate cache cluster nodes: drain, restart worker, restore snapshot.

B) Control-plane write path degraded (etcd/kv higher latency):
- Symptoms: routing updates delayed, deploys hang, alerts from control-plane.
- Action: avoid further config churn. If urgent routing changes needed, use operator-side direct edge-proxy config (out-of-band) documented in emergency-access playbook. Start control-plane recovery flow: scale kv-store, increase timeouts, promote hot-standby. Communicate clearly to incident channel that changes are being made out-of-band and will be reconciled later.

C) Cross-region networking blackhole to ap-south-1:
- Symptoms: SYN timeouts, no healthcheck responses for border proxies.
- Action: Do not reweight traffic TO ap-south-1. If traffic already routed there, immediate soft-reweight away and enable cross-region steer + backfill. File infra ticket with cloud provider and collect tcpdump from border proxies if permitted.

Operator command cheat-sheet (examples):
- Check route stats (last 10m):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${RO_TOKEN}" "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/metrics/route?route=/v1/generate&window=10m"
- Apply delta weight (test):
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${OPERATOR_TOKEN}' -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","change":{"type":"delta","by_region":{"eu-west-1":0.2}},"ttl_seconds":600}' https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/adjust
- Enable variant canary:
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${OPERATOR_TOKEN}' -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","model":"gptx-3-quant-canary","route":"/v1/generate","weight":0.01,"ttl_seconds":1200}' https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/variants/enable
- Rollback weight change (force):
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${OPERATOR_TOKEN}' -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","change":{"type":"reset"}}' https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/reset
- Scale nodepool (k8s example):
  kubectl -n serving scale deployment/gptx-3-gpu --replicas=6

Decision matrix (short):
- If latency spike without errors and cross-region latency within SLO -> prefer soft reweight to healthy region.
- If errors are client-visible (5xx) -> prefer local backfill first, then cross-region steer.
- If control-plane degraded -> do minimal routing changes and prefer out-of-band operator proxy changes.
- If privacy restrictions prevent hosted fallback -> prefer local CPU backfill even if latency higher.

Post-incident checklist:
- Revert all TTL-limited routing deltas or extend them intentionally if change is permanent after review.
- Run automated quality regression on canonical prompt set for any backfilled variant used.
- Capture timeline and link alerts, dashboards, and key commands used.
- Open follow-up Jira tasks for root-cause fixes (eg. cache eviction policy, autoscaler tuning).
- Update runbook with any operator friction points discovered.

Testing and exercises:
- Quarterly chaos drills: simulate 10–15 minute regional degradation and verify staged reweight + backfill flows.
- Test canary activation flows in staging with the same operator commands and TTL semantics.
- Include quality verification step (quick eval harness) to assess backfill regression within 30 minutes of activation.

Open questions / next work items (actionable):
- Define concrete thresholds for automated soft reweight triggers (proposal: 99p latency > 1.3x SLO for 3m -> auto-reweight 10%).
- Add telemetry flag to mark requests served by backfill variants for easier post-incident QA.
- Improve control-plane safe-mode UI to allow single-click TTL-based deltas with prefilled audit reason.

Appendix: useful links and references:
- Incident playbook: confluence/PLATFORM-Incidents/routing-handbook (link above)
- Autoscaler runbook: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/autoscaler/playbook
- Backfill model catalog: confluence/Model-Catalog/backfills

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and operational-first. Feedback wanted on concrete thresholds and whether hosted fallback should be default third step vs final rescue.
- Will iterate with SRE and serving-runtime to add more automation hooks once thresholds agree.
